rows.note: Final model: negative-binomial (NB2) GLM with log link and dispersion parameter alpha fixed at 1 (ML estimation of alpha diverged to a boundary value ~8767 because of extreme zero-inflation, 261/348 quadrats with zero seedlings), with standard errors clustered at Property (18 clusters, small-sample corrected). Outcome: total Eucalyptus seedlings per quadrat-visit, constructed as the sum of the three height-class counts (euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m; validated as identical to the file's euc_sdlgs_all for all rows). Covariates: Season (3 survey rounds, dummies), Euc_canopy_cover (%), log(Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m)+1). Exclusions: listwise deletion of 3 rows with missing grass/canopy/distance values; n = 348 quadrat-visit rows (observation unit = quadrat within a survey round; quadrats not persistent across rounds). Design: 18 properties recurring across 3 rounds, property treated as a clustering level for robust SEs. A Poisson GLMM with property random intercept was attempted first but the variational-Bayes fit failed to converge, triggering this pre-declared NB fallback. Focal effect: coefficient on grass_total = -0.005778 on the log-count scale (IRR per +1 pp grass = 0.994; per +10 pp = 0.944), cluster-robust SE = 0.010306, z = -0.561, 95% CI [-0.0260, +0.0144]; not significant. Sensitivity: NB2 GLM with divergent ML alpha (~8767) gives grass_total = -0.003619 (SE 0.010429, z = -0.347) - same substantive conclusion. Test statistic kind: Wald z (cluster-robust). Inferential df: residual df = 342 for the GLM; clustering df = 18 (properties). Fitted n = 348. Native scale: log mean-count per +1 percentage point of grass cover; no scale conversion applied.

rows.note: Focal model: negative-binomial (NB2, log link) GLM of total Eucalyptus seedlings per 15x15m quadrat (euc_sdlgs_all = sum of the three height-class counts) on summed grass cover, with alpha = 9.11 estimated by NB2 discrete MLE (z_alpha = 7.4, confirming severe overdispersion; Poisson rejected). Predictors: grass cover (% points) = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGraminoid_cover (missing treated as 0; one row all-missing on all four -> NA); covariates Euc_canopy_cover (%) and Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), plus Season fixed effects (Winter 2006/Spring 2006/Autumn 2007). Design: repeated cross-section of 348 quadrats (351 minus 3 rows with missing covariates) nested in 18 properties; quadrats not persistent across rounds, so quadrat is the observation unit and inference uses sandwich SEs clustered on Property (18 clusters). Focal coefficient is the signed partial slope of grass cover on the log-count scale, per +1 percentage point of grass cover: beta = -0.005309, cluster-robust SE = 0.009982, z = -0.532 (large-sample normal), p = 0.595, 95% CI [-0.0249, +0.0143]; df_resid = 342. IRR per +10pp grass = 0.948. Interpretation: higher grass cover is associated with slightly fewer seedlings but the effect is statistically null. Poisson GLM with the same clustered SEs gives a similar estimate (-0.0094, SE 0.0113). Scripts: scripts/01-06. Key contestable choices: (i) grass cover operationalized as sum of all four grass % columns; (ii) recruitment as total count across all size classes; (iii) NB2 over Poisson/zero-inflated alternatives; (iv) clustering instead of property random intercept; (v) no adjustment for bare ground/litter/moss/rock as potential mediators of grass cover.
rows.predictor: Summed grass cover in percentage points of quadrat area (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGraminoid_cover), fitted as a continuous linear term on the log expected seedling count; coefficient reported per +1 percentage point

rows.note: Negative-binomial GEE (log link) with exchangeable working correlation and robust sandwich SEs, clustered on Property (18 clusters; quadrats not persistent across rounds). Outcome: total Eucalyptus seedlings per quadrat (euc_sdlgs_all, all height classes). Focal predictor: total grass cover (%) = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, scaled to 10-percentage-point units; larger value = more grass cover (as_declared). Adjusted for Season (3-level factor), Euc_canopy_cover, and distance to nearest eucalypt canopy (seed-source context). Dropped 3 of 351 rows with missing model variables; n = 348 quadrat-visits, observation unit = one 15x15 m quadrat in one round. Focal estimate = log rate ratio per +10 pp grass cover = -0.0642, robust SE 0.1068, z = -0.601 (p_z = 0.548); small-sample Wald t with df = 18 clusters - 1 = 17: t = -0.601, p = 0.556, 95% CI [-0.289, 0.161]. Sensitivity: Poisson GEE gives same-signed null result (-0.1006, SE 0.1246). Conclusion: no detectable effect of grass cover on seedling recruitment at this sample size; CI spans both moderate negative and moderate positive effects. Design: NB-GEE, exchangeable correlation, cluster-robust inference.
rows.predictor: Total grass cover (% of quadrat) = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, expressed per 10 percentage points; coefficient is the log rate ratio of total eucalypt seedling count per +10 pp grass cover.

Outcome = count of eucalypt seedlings 0–50 cm (euc_sdlgs0_50cm) per 15x15 m quadrat; 88% zeros, max 78. Predictor = total grass percent cover (sum of ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, the only grass-labelled classes; graminoids excluded), scaled to +10 percentage points per unit. Model: GEE negative-binomial (alpha=1, robust sandwich SE, exchangeable within-Property correlation), log(E[count]) ~ grass10 + Euc_canopy_cover + log1p(Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m)) + C(Season, ref Winter 2006), clustered by Property (18 clusters). Exclusions: rows missing any grass cover class (1), canopy cover (1), or distance (2) -> n = 348 of 351. Interpretation: evidence of a negative association but not statistically significant. Sensitivity: alpha in {0.3, 1, 3} gave beta in [-0.221, -0.151] with SE ~0.17-0.21, so inference robust to dispersion choice. Inferential reference: large-sample z (no finite df); observation unit = quadrat-visit; design = clustered cross-sectional survey, properties crossed with 3 survey rounds, quadrats not persistent across rounds.

Dispersion: NB1 alpha = 17.75 estimated by ML (discrete NegativeBinomial fit), passed as fixed alpha to statsmodels GLM; Poisson Pearson dispersion was 15.6, justifying NB. Inference: Property-clustered sandwich standard errors (cov_type='cluster'). Focal result: grass coefficient b = -0.00518 (log scale, per +1 percentage point of grass cover), cluster-robust SE = 0.01003, z = -0.516, p = 0.606, 95% CI [-0.0248, 0.0145] on log scale (rate ratio 0.995, CI [0.975, 1.015]). Observation unit: one 15x15m quadrat in one survey round (quadrats not persistent across rounds; no quadrat random effect possible). rows.note: Negative-binomial (NB2, log-link) GLM of eucalypt seedling counts. Outcome: total eucalypt seedlings per quadrat (sum of euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m; verified equal to euc_sdlgs_all). Focal predictor: total grass cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover (percent of quadrat, linear). Controls: Euc_canopy_cover (linear), Season fixed effects (Autumn 2007 reference), Property fixed effects. Estimand: log-rate-ratio of expected seedling count per +1 percentage point of total grass cover. Complete cases: 351 -> 350 (one row with missing grass/canopy values). From these, three properties (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor) recorded zero seedlings in all quadrats, making their property fixed effects structurally divergent under the log link; they were excluded, giving the focal fit n=300 (15 properties, 3 seasons, one quadrat row per observation). Fit converged via lbfgs (alpha=5.52). Sensitivity: identical model keeping all-zero properties (n=350) gives grass coef -0.00514, SE 0.00945; Newton fits reproduce it, so the estimate is stable. Focal fit: coef=-0.00471, SE=0.00942, z=-0.50, p=0.617, 95% CI [-0.0232, 0.0138]. Test statistic: z (Wald). df: 281 residual (z-test df = n-parameters; quasi-inference). Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round. Design: quadrats nested within 15 properties, crossed with 3 seasonal rounds, property and season as fixed effects. Conclusion: point estimate slightly negative but statistically indistinguishable from zero.

rows.note: MODEL: Negative-binomial (NB2, log link) GLM, dispersion alpha = 9.2 selected by maximizing log-likelihood over a grid (llf = -452.29), with property-clustered sandwich standard errors (18 clusters). OUTCOME: total eucalypt seedlings per quadrat = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m. FOCAL PREDICTOR: total grass percent cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover (percent of quadrat; NativePerennialGraminoid_cover excluded as sedges/rushes are not grasses). COVARIATES: Season (fixed-effect dummies, Autumn 2007 reference), Euc_canopy_cover, Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m). EXCLUSIONS: listwise deletion of the 3 rows missing any grass, canopy-cover, or distance value; fitted n = 348 of 351 quadrats. Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat in one survey round (different quadrats each round; quadrats nested in 18 properties). RESULTS: focal estimate is the grass-cover coefficient on the model's native log count scale, i.e. the log incidence-rate ratio per +1 percentage point of grass cover: -0.00491 (SE 0.01013), z = -0.48, p = 0.63; df: large-sample z inference (no finite df for the sandwich SE; 18 clusters); IRR per +10 percentage points grass = 0.95. Interpretation: no detectable effect of grass cover on Eucalyptus seedling recruitment, though the confidence interval is wide (approx. -0.025 to +0.015 on the log scale per 1pp). Sensitivity: Poisson GLM with property-clustered SEs gives a similar coefficient (-0.0090, SE 0.0113), so the conclusion is not family-dependent. Larger grass-cover values correspond to MORE grass exposure as declared (orientation: as_declared); the negative sign means more grass is associated with slightly (non-significantly) lower recruitment.

Conclusion: no detectable effect of grass cover on Eucalyptus seedling recruitment (IRR per +1pp = 1.007, 95% CI approx 0.990-1.024). rows.note: Primary analysis: negative-binomial GEE with a log link, fitted to the 348 complete-case quadrat-round observations. Outcome was total Eucalyptus seedlings, constructed as euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m. Focal predictor was total true-grass cover, constructed as ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, in percentage points; NativePerennialGraminoid_cover was excluded from the primary predictor. The model included season fixed effects, overhead eucalypt canopy cover, and distance to nearest eucalypt canopy. Properties were treated as clusters with an exchangeable working correlation, and property-clustered robust standard errors were used. Property fixed effects were not used because three properties had no recorded recruitment, which would cause separation. The focal estimate is the log-count change in expected total seedlings for a one-percentage-point increase in total true-grass cover. Test statistic: t = -0.494, df = 17, p = 0.628; 95% CI about (-0.0265, 0.0164). Observation unit: quadrat-round. Design: property-clustered repeated cross-section across Winter 2006, Spring 2006, and Autumn 2007. Sensitivity analyses were consistent with the primary result: a binary any-recruitment GEE gave 0.0024 log-odds per percentage point (SE 0.0082, t = 0.292, df = 17), and a broader grass-plus-graminoid NB GEE gave -0.0053 log-count per percentage point (SE 0.0101, t = -0.521, df = 17). Overall, grass cover showed little evidence of an association with Eucalyptus seedling recruitment.
rows.predictor: Total true-grass cover, defined as ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover, in percentage points of quadrat cover.

rows.note: FOCAL MODEL: Negative-binomial GLM (log link), alpha=7.47 estimated from Poisson Pearson residuals, outcome euc_sdlgs_all (total Eucalyptus seedlings per 15x15 m quadrat visit, 0.50cm-2m and >2m classes summed, precomputed column). FOCAL PREDICTOR: centered total grass cover (percentage points of quadrat ground area) = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGraminoid_cover, mean 31.0, range 0-99. The reported estimate is the log incidence-rate ratio per +1 percentage point of total grass cover: +0.0014 (cluster-robust SE 0.008, z=0.174, p=0.862, 95% CI -0.014 to +0.017). Larger predictor values = more grass cover, so orientation is as_declared. ADJUSTMENT: Euc_canopy_cover, log1p(Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m)), BareGround_cover, Litter_cover, Season fixed effects (Winter/Spring 2006, Autumn 2007); Property handled via 17 property fixed-effect dummies with cluster-robust (by property) standard errors. DESIGN: observation unit = quadrat-visit; nested: 348 quadrat-visits (complete cases; 3 of 351 rows dropped for missing cover/distance values) within 18 named properties (cluster sizes 12-33, mean 19.3); quadrats re-allocated each round (no persistent quadrat IDs). Inferential framework: z-statistic on 339 residual df-equivalent parameters (large-sample Wald, cluster-robust); no small-cluster correction (18 clusters is marginal but cluster-robust SEs are the standard recourse). INFERENCE: no detectable effect of grass cover on seedling recruitment in native scale (log rate-ratio per percentage point). SANITY/ROBUSTNESS: distance to canopy is a stable negative predictor (logdist -0.44, p=0.03), supporting model adequacy. Poisson GEE (exchangeable within property) gave grass_c -0.0104 (SE 0.009) but Pearson dispersion was 17.2, so NB is preferred. Sensitivity: grass excluding graminoid class +0.0022 (SE 0.008); native-vs-exotic grass split natc +0.015 (SE 0.017), exoc -0.004 (SE 0.010); strict 0-50cm-only outcome +0.014 (SE 0.013). All constructions agree on a null effect. Caveat: heavy overdispersion and 74% zero outcomes mean limited power; the CI excludes only large effects (|rate ratio| beyond ~1.7% per percentage point of grass cover).
rows.predictor: Centered total grass percent cover per quadrat (sum of ExoticAnnualGrass_cover, ExoticPerennialGrass_cover, NativePerennialGrass_cover, NativePerennialGraminoid_cover), entered as a single linear term; estimate is the log incidence-rate ratio for total Eucalyptus seedlings per +1 percentage point of grass cover

rows.note: Negative-binomial GLM (log link, Pearson-estimated dispersion alpha = 9.12) of total Eucalyptus seedling count per quadrat (euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m, verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all) on total grass cover (percent; sum of ExoticAnnualGrass_cover, ExoticPerennialGrass_cover, NativePerennialGrass_cover, NativePerennialGraminoid_cover), with Season (3 rounds) as fixed effect and Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m) and Euc_canopy_cover as nuisance covariates. Observation unit: 15x15 m quadrat visit; design: quadrats nested in 18 properties across 3 survey rounds (independent quadrat sets per round). Standard errors cluster-robust, clustered on Property. Listwise deletion of rows missing any model variable: n = 348 of 351. Focal estimate: grass_total coefficient on the model's native log-count scale = -0.00531 per +1 percentage point grass cover (IRR = 0.995), cluster-robust SE = 0.00998, Wald z = -0.532, p = 0.60, 95% CI [-0.025, +0.014]; residual df = 342. Interpretation: no detectable effect of grass cover on seedling recruitment; point estimate slightly negative (more grass = fewer seedlings) but statistically indistinguishable from null. Notable covariate: distance to eucalypt canopy negatively associated with recruitment (z = -2.11). Acknowledged limitation: 74% zero counts; zero-inflation was not modeled separately, relying on NB dispersion + property clustering instead.
rows.predictor: Total grass cover (percent of quadrat), constructed as ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGraminoid_cover; effect reported per +1 percentage point on the log-count scale

rows.note: Model: negative binomial (NB-P, p=2) GLM with log link on total Eucalyptus seedling counts per 15x15 m quadrat (unit = quadrat-visit). Focal predictor: total_grass_cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover (percent of quadrat; there is no native annual grass column), entered as a continuous percent; estimate is the log incidence-rate-ratio per 1 percentage point more grass cover, holding season and property fixed. Fixed effects: Season (3 rounds, Autumn 2007 reference) and Property (18 properties, 17 dummies) absorbing spatial clustering; SEs are cluster-robust sandwich SEs (analytic NB2 scores, inverse-Hessian bread, small-cluster correction G/(G-1)*(N-1)/(N-K-1), G=18 clusters) computed manually because statsmodels NB-P results lack get_robustcov_results. Outcome: total_seedlings = euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m. Exclusions: SurveyID 75 (Rokahr) dropped listwise for missing all grass-cover values; n = 350 (260 zero counts, 90 nonzero). ZINB with property dummies in the inflate part was attempted but non-estimable (singular Hessian); the plain NB-P with cluster-robust SEs is the final, transparent specification. Focal result: coef = -0.00911, cluster-robust SE = 0.0839, z = -0.109, p = 0.914, 95% CI [-0.174, 0.155], log-likelihood = -417.58, alpha = 5.55, df residual = 328. Interpretation: no detectable effect of grass cover on seedling recruitment on the native log-rate scale; precision is limited because most variance in recruitment is within-property (cluster-robust SE is ~9x the model-based SE). Test statistic: z (Wald, two-sided), value -0.109. Orientation: as_declared (larger total grass cover = more of the grass-cover exposure the estimand is oriented on; the estimated sign is negative). Design: nested field survey, 18 properties x 3 seasons, unique random quadrats per round; observation unit is one quadrat in one round.
rows.predictor: total_grass_cover = percent of quadrat in grass (ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover), per 1 percentage point; effect on log seedling count rate

rows.note: Negative-binomial (NB2) regression, log link, alpha estimated by MLE = 8.78, fitted with property-clustered sandwich SEs (18 clusters). Outcome: euc_sdlgs_all (total eucalypt seedlings per 15x15 m quadrat, all height classes). Focal predictor: grass_cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover (percent points of quadrat; no native annual grass column exists; NativePerennialGraminoid_cover excluded as graminoid, not grass). Covariates: Euc_canopy_cover, distance to nearest eucalypt canopy (m), Litter_cover, BareGround_cover, Season fixed effects. Complete-case deletion: 3 of 351 rows dropped, n=348; observation unit = one quadrat-visit; quadrats not resampled across rounds. Focal estimate on native scale: log count-ratio per 1 pp grass cover = 0.00248, cluster SE 0.00834, t(17) = 0.298, p = 0.77, 95% CI [-0.01512, 0.02009] (rate ratio 1.0025 per pp) — a precise null. Overdispersion: Poisson Pearson dispersion 15.0; fixed-alpha NB (13.96) gave +0.0031 (SE 0.0084); Poisson cluster-robust estimate -0.0098 (SE 0.0094) lies inside the NB CI, sign difference attributable to overdispersion weighting. Conclusion: after accounting for seed-source distance, canopy, competing ground covers, season, and property clustering, grass cover shows no detectable effect on seedling recruitment in these data. Scripts: scripts/01-04.

rows.note: Negative binomial (NB2, log link) count model: y = total Eucalyptus seedling count per 15x15 m quadrat visit (sum of euc_sdlgs0_50cm, euc_sdlgs50cm_2m, euc_sdlgs>2m). Focal predictor: total grass cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover (percent of quadrat; no native annual grass column exists in the data). Adjusted for Euc_canopy_cover, Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), and Season (factor, reference Autumn 2007). Complete-case analysis, n = 348 of 351 rows (3 dropped for missing grass values; seedling counts complete). Dispersion parameter alpha = 9.12 estimated by ML (Poisson dispersion check was 6.87, justifying NB). Standard errors clustered by Property (18 clusters). Focal estimate: grass coefficient beta = -0.00491 on the log-count scale, i.e., each additional percentage point of quadrat grass cover multiplies expected seedling count by exp(-0.00491) = 0.9951. Test statistic: z = -0.485 (two-sided p = 0.63, normal reference distribution as standard for ML count models); model residual df = 342 (n=348 minus 6 regression parameters). Observation unit: one quadrat sampled in one survey round (quadrats not revisited). Result: no detectable effect of grass cover on eucalypt seedling recruitment at this adjustment level; the strongest predictor in the model was distance to eucalypt canopy (beta = -0.0298, z = -2.12).
rows.predictor: Total grass cover: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover (percent of quadrat ground area), entered as a continuous predictor; estimate is the log count-ratio of total eucalypt seedlings per one percentage-point increase in grass cover.

rows.note: Focal model: negative binomial GLM with log link (dispersion alpha profiled by grid-ML to 8.87), fitted to n=348 complete-case quadrats in 18 properties (3 rows dropped for missing grass cover, canopy cover, or canopy distance). Outcome: euc_sdlgs_all = total Eucalyptus seedling count across all three height classes (0-50cm, 50cm-2m, >2m; file's precomputed total, verified equal to class sum). Predictors: grass (focal, see predictor field), Euc_canopy_cover (%), Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m) (seed-source confounder controls), C(Season) (3 rounds, Winter 2006 reference). Standard errors clustered on Property (18 clusters) to account for the nested design; statsmodels formula-GLM does not fit a true GLMM, so clustering handles within-property correlation while alpha handles overdispersion (variance >> mean justified NB over Poisson). Focal estimate: log count ratio per +1 percentage point of grass cover = -0.00492 (rate ratio 0.995 per +1% grass), cluster-robust SE 0.01012, z = -0.486, p = 0.627; inference is asymptotic (z, no finite df); residual df 342. Test statistic kind: z = -0.486. Observation unit: 15x15m quadrat-visit. Design: quadrats nested within 18 properties, 3 survey rounds, quadrats not persistent across rounds. Sensitivity analyses (identical structure, Property-clustered SEs): recent-recruitment outcome euc_sdlgs0_50cm gives b=-0.0123 (se 0.0103, p=0.231); exotic grasses only b=-0.0127 (se 0.0106, p=0.229); native perennial grass alone b=+0.0067 (se 0.0177, p=0.704) — the total-grass null is not masking offsetting component effects. Conclusion: no detectable effect of grass cover on Eucalyptus seedling recruitment in this survey; the estimate is slightly negative with a wide CI (95% CI approx -0.025 to +0.015 log count ratio per +1% grass).
rows.predictor: Total grass cover, in percentage points of quadrat ground area: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover (no native annual grass class exists in the data). The reported effect is the log count-ratio of total Eucalyptus seedlings per +1 percentage point of this summed grass cover, on the model's native log scale.
